question.worked_solution:
To solve this equation, we need both exponential terms to have a common base.

To do this, we write $125$ as ${5}^{3},$ and then rewrite the right-hand side using the power rule of exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{m-10} & ={125}^{m} \\ {5}^{m-10} & ={({5}^{3})}^{m} \\ {5}^{m-10} & ={5}^{3m}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(5)$, we equate the exponents and solve for $m:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m-10 & =3m \\ -2m & =10 \\ m & =-5\end{aligned}
$$
